actions.name: Exploit public-facing networking devices to gain initial access
actions.description: The Iranian cyber actors exploit vulnerabilities in public-facing networking devices such as Citrix Netscaler, F5 BIG-IP, Pulse Secure/Ivanti VPNs, PanOS firewalls, and Check Point Security Gateways to gain initial access to victim networks.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Catalogue has no exact component/version and safe validation mapping for this action; provide the target software, version, and expected evidence.

actions.name: Use Shodan search engine to identify vulnerable IP addresses
actions.description: The actors use the Shodan search engine to identify and enumerate IP addresses hosting devices vulnerable to particular CVEs.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Catalogue has no exact component/version and safe validation mapping for this action; provide the target software, version, and expected evidence.

actions.name: Deploy webshells on compromised Citrix Netscaler devices
actions.description: The actors deploy webshells on compromised Citrix Netscaler devices, including creating directories and placing files such as netscaler.1, netscaler.php, ctxHeaderLogon.php, and others for credential capture and persistence.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The target host has no deployable service, so it is left out of deployment; this step is not reproduced until a service or substitute is supplied for that host.

actions.name: Create accounts on victim networks
actions.description: The actors create local accounts on victim networks with observed names including sqladmin$, adfsservice, IIS_Admin, iis-admin, and John McCain.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Request exemptions to zero-trust application and security policies
actions.description: The actors request exemptions to zero-trust application and security policies for tools they intend to deploy on victim networks.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The environment can be built (NGINX), but this step is not about that software and has no step-specific reproduction or validation; it remains untested.

actions.name: Create malicious scheduled task using DLL side-loading technique
actions.description: The actors create a malicious scheduled task named SpaceAgentTaskMgrSHR in Windows/Spaceport/task folder that uses DLL side-loading against contig.exe (renamed to dllhost.ext) to load a payload from version.dll executed from the Windows Downloads directory.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Place malicious backdoor version.dll in C:\Windows\ADFS\ directory
actions.description: The actors place a malicious backdoor file named version.dll in the C:\Windows\ADFS\ directory.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Use scheduled tasks to load malware through installed backdoors
actions.description: The actors use scheduled tasks to load malware through installed backdoors for persistence.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Catalogue has no exact component/version and safe validation mapping for this action; provide the target software, version, and expected evidence.

actions.name: Deploy Meshcentral for remote access
actions.description: The actors deploy Meshcentral to connect with compromised servers for remote access.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Create daily Windows service task with random name for persistence
actions.description: The actors create a daily Windows service task with a random eight-character name and attempt execution of a similarly named DLL in C:\Windows\system32\drivers\ directory for persistence.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Repurpose compromised credentials to log into other applications
actions.description: The actors repurpose compromised credentials from exploited networking devices such as Citrix Netscaler to log into other applications like Citrix XenDesktop.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Catalogue has no exact component/version and safe validation mapping for this action; provide the target software, version, and expected evidence.

actions.name: Repurpose administrative credentials to log into domain controllers and infrastructure
actions.description: The actors repurpose administrative credentials of network administrators to log into domain controllers and other infrastructure on victim networks.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The environment can be built (NGINX), but this step is not about that software and has no step-specific reproduction or validation; it remains untested.

actions.name: Disable antivirus and security software using administrator credentials
actions.description: The actors use administrator credentials to disable antivirus and security software on victim networks.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The environment can be built (NGINX), but this step is not about that software and has no step-specific reproduction or validation; it remains untested.

actions.name: Lower PowerShell policies to a less secure level
actions.description: The actors lower PowerShell policies to a less secure level to evade defenses.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Catalogue has no exact component/version and safe validation mapping for this action; provide the target software, version, and expected evidence.

actions.name: Attempt to enter security exemption tickets to get tools allowlisted
actions.description: The actors attempt to enter security exemption tickets to the network security device or contractor to get their tools allowlisted.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Catalogue has no exact component/version and safe validation mapping for this action; provide the target software, version, and expected evidence.

actions.name: Initiate remote desktop session using compromised administrator account
actions.description: The actors use a compromised administrator account to initiate a remote desktop session to another server on the network and attempt to start Microsoft Windows PowerShell ISE to run commands.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Export system registry hives and network firewall configurations
actions.description: The actors export system registry hives and network firewall configurations on compromised servers for discovery.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Exfiltrate account usernames and access configuration files and logs
actions.description: The actors exfiltrate account usernames from the victim domain controller and access configuration files and logs to gather network and user account information for further exploitation.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Install AnyDesk remote access program as backup access
actions.description: The actors install the AnyDesk remote access program as a backup access method on compromised systems.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Catalogue has no exact component/version and safe validation mapping for this action; provide the target software, version, and expected evidence.

actions.name: Enable Windows PowerShell Web Access on servers
actions.description: The actors enable servers to use Windows PowerShell Web Access for command and control.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Use Ligolo and NGROK for tunneling and outbound connections
actions.description: The actors use the open source tunneling tool Ligolo (ligolo/ligolo-ng) and NGROK (ngrok[.]io) to create outbound connections to random subdomains for command and control.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Catalogue has no exact component/version and safe validation mapping for this action; provide the target software, version, and expected evidence.

actions.name: Collaborate with ransomware affiliates to enable ransomware attacks
actions.description: After infiltrating victim networks, the actors collaborate with ransomware affiliates including NoEscape, Ransomhouse, and ALPHV (BlackCat) by providing access, locking victim networks, and strategizing extortion in exchange for a percentage of ransom payments.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The environment can be built (NGINX), but this step is not about that software and has no step-specific reproduction or validation; it remains untested.

evidence.quote: The Iranian cyber actors’ initial intrusions rely upon exploits of remote external services on internet-facing assets to gain initial access to victim networks. As of July 2024, these actors have been observed scanning IP addresses hosting Check Point Security Gateways, probing for devices potentially vulnerable to CVE-2024-24919. As of April 2024, these actors have conducted mass scanning of IP addresses hosting Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS and GlobalProtect VPN devices. The actors were likely conducting reconnaissance and probing for devices vulnerable to CVE-2024-3400. Historically, this group has exploited organizations by leveraging CVE-2019-19781 and CVE-2023-3519 related to Citrix Netscaler, and CVE-2022-1388 related to BIG-IP F5 devices.
